reason: The cited evidence supports that laser cladding can produce metallurgically bonded HEA coatings with low dilution and good wear resistance on steel substrates, but none of the passages directly address hot-cracking suppression, comparative performance against fusion-welding repair, or behavior under cyclic loading. The key premise that rapid solidification suppresses hot cracking is not supported by the cited studies.
premises: Laser cladding of HEA coatings on H13 steel yields metallurgical bonding and low dilution
Rapid solidification during laser cladding suppresses hot cracking
HEA coatings (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi-based) provide enhanced wear resistance at elevated temperatures
The proposed coating system is effective under high-temperature, cyclic loading conditions
Laser-clad HEA repair outperforms traditional fusion-welding repair in reducing hot cracking
